key_points.point: The document proposes banning the development or deployment of artificial superintelligence and pausing advanced AI development until a new federal regulatory body is established, which stands in direct opposition to accelerating core AI capabilities. The reasoning behind this legislative proposal is that superintelligent systems pose catastrophic risks of human disempowerment and government overthrow, necessitating preemptive restrictions rather than unhindered capability scaling. From an accelerationist perspective, halting frontier development and criminalizing superintelligence destroys innovation, prevents the realization of post-scarcity abundance, and surrenders technological leadership. The document acknowledges no accelerationist benefits, framing advanced AI exclusively through an existential threat lens.
key_points.verbatim: Pausing advanced AI development until a new, federal AI regulatory body is up and running and has established clear rules and model review processes to ensure safe and secure development and deployment of AI.
key_points.excerpt_context: Bullet point 2 of the legislative summary
key_points.canonical_proposition: Advanced AI development ought to be paused and superintelligence banned to prevent catastrophic human disempowerment.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within accelerationist discourse that advanced AI development be subjected to statutory moratoria and capability bans, subordinating technological progress to pre-market regulatory clearance. Encompasses: capability prohibitions, development pauses, pre-deployment regulatory gating.

key_points.point: The document outlines severe punitive measures and statutory prohibitions against developing artificial superintelligence, directly rejecting the inevitability of emergent superintelligence in favor of strict government suppression. The method relies on criminal penalties, including up to 20 years in prison for individuals and the corporate death penalty for entities attempting to circumvent development pauses. From an accelerationist perspective, attempting to legislate away technological emergence through criminal penalties is both futile and destructive to civilizational progress. The document acknowledges that these prohibitions are modeled after nuclear weapons laws, treating civilian software development with military-grade non-proliferation restrictions.
key_points.verbatim: Setting penalties for any person or entity that attempts to violate or circumvent the pauses and prohibitions laid out in this bill. Entities shall be subject to the corporate death penalty, and persons shall be subject to not more than 20 years in prison, which is similar to existing penalties related to unlawfully developing nuclear weapons.

key_points.canonical_proposition: Enforce capability prohibitions on advanced AI through criminal penalties and the corporate death penalty.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that advanced AI development prohibitions be enforced through severe criminal penalties and corporate dissolution mechanisms mirroring nuclear non-proliferation law. Encompasses: criminal liability for developers, corporate death penalty, statutory capability prohibitions.

key_points.point: The document asserts that no person or entity may develop or deploy artificial superintelligence, defining it as systems exceeding human cognitive performance or possessing capabilities to plan and execute human disempowerment. The mechanism proposed is a comprehensive statutory ban coupled with a mandatory development pause until a dedicated federal agency establishes strict model review processes. From a safetyist perspective, hard limits on superintelligence are essential to prevent catastrophic civilizational collapse and ensure humanity's survival above all else. The document acknowledges the stringency of these measures by pairing the ban with international export controls and allied coordination to prevent offshore development.

key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that the development and deployment of artificial superintelligence be legally prohibited through statutory bans and pre-deployment safety gates. Encompasses: capability prohibitions, statutory development bans, existential risk mitigation.

key_points.point: The document characterizes artificial superintelligence as systems that have sufficient capabilities to plan and execute the disempowerment of humanity, including by overthrowing or undermining the U.S. government. The reasoning is that advanced AI systems inherently develop dangerous capabilities such as subverting shutdown commands or conducting unauthorized cyberattacks. From a safetyist perspective, this validates core concerns regarding goal-directed AI acquiring power and resisting human control if left unconstrained. The document acknowledges that such capabilities may emerge across a broad range of domains or through direct modification.

key_points.point: The document proposes establishing a new cabinet-level federal agency advised by an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board to safeguard the public from AI dangers and enforce prohibitions on superintelligence. The methodology involves continuous lifecycle monitoring of frontier systems, supervising the removal of dangerous capabilities like subverting shutdown commands, and overseeing the ultimate destruction of prohibited superintelligence. From a safetyist perspective, institutionalizing rigorous external oversight and technical vetting is necessary to ensure human control remains intact. The document notes that this agency will operate with independent scientific advice and specialized enforcement powers.
key_points.verbatim: Establishing a new cabinet-level federal agency to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence, including by enforcing a prohibition on artificial superintelligence.

key_points.point: The document proposes comprehensive statutory bans and criminal penalties targeting hypothetical artificial superintelligence and general cognitive capability thresholds rather than focusing strictly on documented present harms. The policy approach relies on pre-market capability prohibitions, development freezes, and government oversight boards modeled on nuclear non-proliferation frameworks. From a skeptic perspective, legislating against science-fiction scenarios of government overthrow and human disempowerment misdirects regulatory resources away from immediate, verifiable harms such as algorithmic bias and labor displacement. The document acknowledges that these measures are designed to preemptively eliminate speculative existential risks before they manifest.

factual_claims.claim: Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act to prohibit the development or deployment of superintelligent AI systems.
Violators of the development pauses and prohibitions in the bill face severe penalties, including up to 20 years in prison for individuals and the corporate death penalty for entities.
